title: Agentic Screening in Equilibrium
authors: with Brian Jabarian, Mariya Pominova, and Pëllumb Reshidi
description: How does AI screening change hiring when firms compete for workers? We combine a randomized experiment with approximately 70,000 applicants in the Philippines and a model of competing firms to study screening, the similarity of evaluations, and the equilibrium effects of AI adoption.

title: AI, Firm Learning, and Internal Labor Markets
description: I study how better prediction technologies change what firms learn about their workers and how that information shapes promotions, separations, and wages. The project combines a model of employer learning with evidence on AI exposure and careers within firms.

title: Technology Adoption across Space and Industries
description: Why do technologies that can be used in many places diffuse unevenly across locations and industries? I study how local adoption costs and economic structure shape technology diffusion and its aggregate and distributional effects, drawing on historical evidence from industrial technology adoption.

title: The Origins of Innovation Clusters
authors: with Gaurav Khanna and Yuhei Miyauchi
description: We use linked patent and career data to study the people, firms, and places behind innovation clusters. Current work examines inventor mobility, workplace sorting, and the role of universities in local innovation, including graduate labor supply and university–firm research links.
